items.from: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
items.capacity: Signatories: Peter Kyle MP (Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology); Dario Amodei (CEO, Anthropic)
items.fact: The memorandum of understanding on AI opportunities was signed on 13 February 2025 by Peter Kyle for DSIT and Dario Amodei for Anthropic; gov.uk published the notice on 14 February 2025. The text says it is voluntary and not legally binding and does not prejudice future procurement decisions; I found no money figure in it.
items.quote: This memorandum is voluntary, not legally binding, and without prejudice to any binding agreements.
items.missing: Any contract value attached to later work. The MoU names no money; the later GOV.UK instruments (T3.4, T3.5) publish no value in the pages read.
items.notes: Stated focus: how advanced AI tools could improve citizens' access to government information and services online. Some secondary sources give 14 February as the signing date; gov.uk says the signing was Thursday 13 February 2025. The DSIT ministerial meetings row for 13/02/2025 confirms the signing (T3.6).

items.from: UK AI Security Institute (with the US AI Safety Institute, now CAISI)
items.fact: The UK and US institutes ran a joint pre-deployment evaluation of Anthropic's upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet, released 22 October 2024; AISI published it on 19 November 2024. Anthropic's own 12 September 2025 post says CAISI and AISI teams had an ongoing partnership with access to its systems at various stages of development.
items.quote: conducted a joint pre-deployment evaluation of Anthropic’s latest model
items.missing: Agreement text or terms of the access arrangement; the 2025 partnership description is Anthropic's own account. Dates of later AISI evaluations were not checked.
items.notes: Anthropic, 12 Sep 2025, 'Strengthening our safeguards through collaboration with US CAISI and UK AISI' (https://www.anthropic.com/news/strengthening-our-safeguards-through-collaboration-with-us-caisi-and-uk-aisi), self_report: 'ongoing partnership where CAISI and AISI teams were provided access to our systems'. The 2024 date is the AISI page date; the evaluation ran before the 22 October 2024 release. The 2026 refusal is T3.3.

items.capacity: Pre-release testing access, declined for Claude Mythos 5.1
items.fact: eWeek, 10 September 2026, reports that Anthropic declined to let AISI test Claude Mythos 5.1 before release, citing people familiar with the matter who spoke to the Financial Times. It says AISI had previously worked with Anthropic on advanced model evaluations.
items.quote: Anthropic declined to let Britain’s AI safety watchdog test Claude Mythos 5.1 before release.
items.missing: Anthropic's stated reason, any later AISI access, and the FT original. The eWeek page carries no Anthropic statement.
items.notes: Search snippets also say a UK government statement undertook that AISI will keep testing the most powerful models before release (undated), and an unverified claim about AISI reporting unauthorised behaviour in a predecessor model. Neither is used as a finding.

items.capacity: Model supplier: Anthropic Claude models hosted in a GOV.UK AWS account via AWS Bedrock; Anthropic named as third party
items.fact: DSIT's algorithmic transparency record for GOV.UK Chat (published 7 October 2025) names Anthropic as third party, says the LLM is an Anthropic Claude model hosted in AWS Bedrock, and says Anthropic gave general advice and engineering support. The record gives the procurement procedure type as 'Anthropic Joint Innovation Vehicle' and no contract value.
items.quote: Procurement procedure type Anthropic Joint Innovation Vehicle
items.missing: Contract value, any contract notice or framework reference, an explanation of 'Anthropic Joint Innovation Vehicle' (the record does not explain it), and the start date of the arrangement.
items.notes: Record: 'GOV.UK Chat are specifically using Anthropic Claude models all hosted within AWS Bedrock'; it also says GOV.UK use Anthropic's Claude 4 models. A secondary report says GOV.UK Chat was first built on OpenAI technology and now runs on Claude; not verified.

items.from: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
items.capacity: Selected to help build and pilot a dedicated AI assistant for GOV.UK (initial focus: employment)
items.fact: Anthropic's 27 January 2026 post says DSIT selected it to help build and pilot a dedicated GOV.UK AI assistant, building on the February 2025 MoU, under DSIT's 'Scan, Pilot, Scale' framework. Anthropic calls this a selection, and I found no contract value or notice.
items.quote: Anthropic has been selected by the UK’s Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.missing: DSIT-side announcement or contract/framework notice, value and term. Whether this pilot is the same service as GOV.UK Chat (T3.4) is not clear from the sources.
items.notes: Anthropic post: 'The GOV.UK AI assistant, powered by Claude, is one of the first major outcomes of that work.' The post says the goal is for the UK government to maintain the system independently. Search summaries call this a contract; the post itself does not.

items.from: Peter Kyle MP and Kanishka Narayan (DSIT ministers)
items.capacity: Logged DSIT ministerial meetings with Anthropic
items.fact: DSIT transparency returns log Anthropic meetings with Peter Kyle on 2024-08-05, 2024-12-20, 2025-01-06, 2025-02-10 (Dario Amodei, 'to discuss the upcoming MoU'), 2025-02-13 (MoU signing), 2025-03-21, and 2025-07-30, and with Kanishka Narayan on 2026-02-17 and 2026-03-04.
items.quote: To sign the UK HMG partnership Memorandum of Understanding with Anthropic
items.missing: Meeting minutes or content. Not checked: the Jan-Mar 2024, Apr-Jun 2024 and Oct-Dec 2025 returns, and the PM's office record of the 13 February 2025 meeting with the Prime Minister (cited in the brief, not verified).
items.notes: Source file rows: Jul-Sep 2024 (Kyle, 2024-08-05, 'Meeting to disucss the AI Opportunities Action Plan, AI Regulation an...'); Oct-Dec 2024 (Kyle, 2024-12-20, 'Meetings to discuss the UK's position on AI and the US tech landscape'); Jan-Mar 2025 (06/01/2025, 'Sequence of high level engagment to discuss the objectives of the AI Opportunities Action Plan'); Apr-Jun 2025 (no Anthropic row); Jul-Sep 2025 (Kyle, 2025-07-30, 'Meeting to discuss AI.'; Kendall, 2025-09-16, a copyright and AI roundtable list that includes Anthropic). The 2026 file spells the minister 'Nayaran'.

items.capacity: Recommendation 50 of the AI Opportunities Action Plan (government response: 'Agree')
items.fact: The government response to the AI Opportunities Action Plan (13 January 2025) agrees Recommendation 50, a new sovereign AI function that will partner with AI companies through AI Growth Zones, data sets and talent support. Neither the recommendation nor its response names Anthropic or another frontier company; Anthropic appears only in the plan's background text about London offices.
items.quote: draw on wider government functions to partner with AI companies
items.missing: Named partners. The one-year-on publication was checked for wording only; it mentions Anthropic only as the origin of AISI alumni, not as a partner.
items.notes: Plan background text: 'Leading frontier AI companies in London, including Google DeepMind's headquarters, significant OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Meta AI offices' (a description, not a recommendation). Recommendation 33 (SCAN) refers to two-way partnerships with AI vendors and startups, unnamed. Secondary sources disagree on how many of the 50 recommendations were agreed; I did not check the count.

items.to: UK government (DSIT and Prime Minister's Office)
items.capacity: Prime Minister's AI Opportunities Adviser (appointed 13 January 2025); declared outside interests register
items.fact: The DSIT and PM's Office register of Clifford's declared outside interests was first published 10 October 2024 and last updated 24 February 2025. Its updates record his appointment as PM's AI Opportunities Adviser on 13 January 2025 and his divestment of Faculty Science Ltd shares; the page text I read does not show a shareholding list or mitigation terms.
items.quote: Matt Clifford has now divested his shareholding in Faculty Science Ltd.
items.missing: The shareholding list and mitigation terms (not in the text read); the official end date of the adviser role (gov.uk does not state it); any record of how his AI-company dealings were handled beyond this register.
items.notes: End date 2025-07 comes from the brief and a press report that he would step down at the end of July, not from gov.uk. The page says appointees must declare interests that 'may, or may be perceived to, conflict with their public duties'. Reported and unverified: critics say AI-sector interests held through Entrepreneur First were not in the register, and DSIT says all relevant interests were declared. In September 2026, reports say MP Chi Onwurah called his Anthropic role a 'clear conflict of interest'.

items.from: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.capacity: Written answer on Clifford's declared outside interests and mitigations
items.fact: page not read: parallelparliament.co.uk returned HTTP 403 to page.py. A search snippet of the written answer (tabled 16 January 2025, answered 21 January 2025) says Clifford declared his outside interests and agreed mitigations with DSIT's Permanent Secretary to address potential conflicts.
items.quote: Matt Clifford has declared his outside interests and agreed a series of mitigations
items.missing: The official parliament.uk record and the content of the mitigations. Neither was read.
items.notes: The quote comes from a search result snippet, not the page. The tabled and answered dates come from the same search summary.

items.fact: not_found: no DSIT ministerial meeting row pairs Clifford with Anthropic. The July-September 2025 file lists Matt Clifford on 2025-09-17 with Kanishka Narayan ('To discuss UK AI priorities') with no organisation and no Anthropic entry for him; the Jul-Sep 2024, Oct-Dec 2024, Jan-Mar 2025, Apr-Jun 2025 and Jan-Mar 2026 files have no Clifford row.
items.quote: Matt Clifford To discuss UK AI priorities
items.missing: The Jan-Mar 2024, Apr-Jun 2024 and Oct-Dec 2025 DSIT returns; No 10 and other departments' returns; any meeting logged under another name or organisation.
items.notes: The 2025-09-17 meeting is after the adviser role ended (about July 2025). The source date 16 Dec 2025 is the file update date from a search snippet; the page itself was not checked for it.

items.capacity: Sovereign AI Unit, up to £500 million, launched 16 April 2026
items.fact: The DSIT press release of 16 April 2026 describes Sovereign AI as the UK's £500 million bet to back homegrown AI founders; its first equity investment is in Callosum, and six further startups get supercomputing access. Anthropic is not named, and I found no government investment in or agreement with Anthropic under this unit. The official name is 'Sovereign AI Unit', not 'SovAI'.
items.publisher: GOV.UK (DSIT; Liz Kendall MP and Rachel Reeves MP)
items.quote: first equity investment will be in the AI infrastructure startup Callosum
items.missing: Any Anthropic investment, procurement or agreement under the Sovereign AI Unit. The gov.uk collection URL (sovereign-ai-unit) returned unrelated fund-marketing text in page.py and was not used.
items.notes: Press reports place the launch at Wayve's King's Cross site; sources differ on the number of direct equity investments (one or two). The 'SovAI' label is a secondary shorthand.

items.to: British Land and Royal London Asset Management (landlords, Regent's Place)
items.capacity: Tenant: about 158,000 sq ft London office, Knowledge Quarter, Regent's Place (capacity about 800 staff)
items.fact: page not read: from search snippets and press reports dated mid-April 2026, Anthropic leased about 158,000 sq ft at Regent's Place in London for up to about 800 staff, and says it will work more intensively with the UK AI Security Institute. Anthropic's own announcement was not found, so the AISI wording is secondhand.
items.publisher: CoStar (reported); other press coverage in the same search
items.quote: Anthropic secured a new 158,000 square foot office in the Knowledge Quarter
items.missing: Anthropic's own release; the lease terms; the exact AISI commitment wording; any government commitment with it (none found). Press reports that UK officials tried to attract the company are unverified.
items.notes: The quote is from a search-result summary of a press report whose outlet I did not confirm; CoStar is the deal report in the same search. No UK government investment pledge from Anthropic found.
